clue.text: 21 at one point causing fights

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, to tease, also means to comb, as when backcombing hair
taken as written
S, south, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone at one point teases, and that teasing sparks fights.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer at 21 across; to tease hair is to comb it.
explanation.definitionFit: Combats are battles or struggles, the same as fights.

clue.text: Brown's after international players — much may turn on this

indicators.note: after puts the brown shade following the players

parts.note: caps are players capped for their country
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A man called Brown follows the national team, and plenty depends on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship that hauls cable, so a lot literally turns on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating winch on which heavy cables are wound.

clue.text: Leaves lying around a bill for biscuits

indicators.note: the stranding word lies around the abbreviation for an account

parts.note: to maroon is to leave stranded
a/c, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Foliage strewn about an invoice for some cookies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage, but it is the verb maroons.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroons are small almond biscuits or cookies.

clue.text: She'll have one's heart in time

indicators.note: in places that central letter inside the word for a long time

parts.note: ages means a long time

indicators.note: heart means the middle letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A woman who will regain her courage eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's heart' is the N in the middle of ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's name, so a female person.

clue.text: Place the queen's given a paper-seller

parts.note: a station is a place or post
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A newsagent is set up in a location by royal favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer sells writing paper and office supplies.

clue.text: Diplomatic in the main

definitions.meaning: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea, here the largest ocean

explanation.surface: Someone is tactful for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly', but 'the main' is the sea; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peace-making, hence diplomatic, and is also the name of the world's biggest ocean, the main.

clue.text: Quietly dress and make a search

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: Someone dresses without a sound and then hunts around.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate or explore, to search into something.

clue.text: Many a hanging's ordered for convicted men

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, is many

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A judge has sentenced several prisoners to death.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of prisoners chained together for labour.

clue.text: Sneak in, having nothing in hand

indicators.note: in hand means put inside the word for a hand

parts.note: a fist is a closed hand
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A thief slips inside with empty hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist is to slip something in deceitfully, palming it off.

clue.text: Retreat to study an opening

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A recluse withdraws to read about a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a religious house, a place of retreat for nuns.

clue.text: The nut taking exercise is able

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A crazy person who starts working out turns out to be capable.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is a kind of nut from a hickory tree.

clue.text: Love can get a girl into trouble

parts.note: A plus DORA, a girl's name

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of 'into' are stirred up

explanation.surface: A warning that romance can leave a young woman pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface warns of pregnancy, but 'trouble' is the anagram signal, and 'can get' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep devoted affection, a form of love.

clue.text: This keeps people from going straight in

definitions.text: This keeps people from going straight in

parts.words: This keeps people from going straight in
parts.note: a rotating barrier at an entrance makes each person turn as they pass through, one at a time

explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving gate admitting people singly, so nobody walks straight through.

clue.text: A slice of brawn — it really needs salt

indicators.note: A slice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook complains that a piece of pressed meat is underseasoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Brawn is a British cold meat made from pig's head set in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is saltpetre, potassium nitrate, a salt.

clue.text: Gin can make one so tipsy!

indicators.note: being tipsy makes one unsteady, so the letters of 'one so' reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a drink of gin can make a person tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin is not the drink but a trap for game, as in gin trap; 'can make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, and a noose is a looped snare.

clue.text: Clear one troublesome pest seen in the river

indicators.note: seen in means put within the name of the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
taken as written
a rat is a troublesome pest

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a nuisance animal spotted in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to declare free from blame, to clear of guilt.

clue.text: Modern buying and selling is just a game

parts.note: new means modern
a market is where buying and selling go on

explanation.surface: A cynic dismisses modern commerce as nothing more than play.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a card game, and also an English horse-racing town; 'is just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a card game played with a stake laid on certain cards.

clue.text: They have to come to grips with the opposition

definitions.text: They have to come to grips with the opposition

parts.words: They have to come to grips with the opposition
parts.note: reads like politicians tackling rivals, but it is literal grappling on a mat

explanation.definitionFit: Grapplers in a bout must physically grasp their opponents.

clue.text: His every contact was of enormous value

definitions.text: His every contact was of enormous value

parts.words: His every contact was of enormous value
parts.note: reads like a well-connected businessman, but every touch turned things to gold in the Greek myth

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Phrygian ruler had a golden touch, turning all he touched to gold.

clue.text: The underworld way — or the converse

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a course is a way or route

explanation.surface: A path through hell, or perhaps its exact opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the converse' looks like 'the opposite', but converse is a noun for talk; 'or the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse and converse both mean conversation or spoken exchange.

clue.text: The US lawman on the list is worth meeting

parts.note: DA, District Attorney, a US prosecutor
a table is a list or chart

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor named on the roster is someone you would like to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the lawman above the list in a down clue; 'The', 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Datable describes someone suitable to go out with romantically.

clue.text: Person taken in by Greek has-been

indicators.note: being taken in by the abbreviation for Greek means sitting inside it

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one should'

explanation.surface: Somebody conned by a Greek turns out to be past it.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone finished or doomed, much like a has-been.

clue.text: In a bad state due to a reckless driver?

definitions.meaning: knocked over by a vehicle, as a careless motorist might do

explanation.definitionFit: Run-down means shabby or exhausted, and to be run down is to be hit by a car.

clue.text: Occasion some irritation with sound refreshments

indicators.note: sound means we hear the word for refreshments said out loud

parts.note: teas are light refreshments, afternoon teas

explanation.surface: Healthy refreshments somehow cause annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' reads as 'healthy', but it signals the homophone; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease someone is to provoke or annoy them, to cause mild irritation.

clue.text: One publicising a clothes-drier

definitions.meaning: someone who airs views or broadcasts things

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who airs opinions broadcasts them, and a rack for drying washing is also so named.

clue.text: An American stock holder

parts.note: reads like an investor holding shares, but the stock is livestock on a ranch

explanation.definitionFit: A rancher in the US owns herds of livestock, which is stock of a different kind.

clue.text: Work in bed, so put on board

indicators.note: in places the work inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
op, opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A lazy executive does his job from bed and gets a board seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-opt is to appoint someone to a committee or board by the members' vote.

clue.text: Left near-ruined in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of 'near' are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A place left almost in ruins in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near-ruined' reads as 'nearly ruined', but 'near' is the fodder; Larne is a port town in County Antrim.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a ferry port on the Antrim coast of Ulster.

clue.text: A song — a song sung in winter in the nude!

indicators.note: in the nude means placed inside the word for naked

parts.note: bare means nude
a carol is a song sung at Christmas time

explanation.surface: A tune that someone sings naked in the freezing cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a boating song of Venetian gondoliers.

clue.text: The show sent on mid-October

parts.note: rode means travelled on, was carried along

indicators.note: mid- picks the centre letter of the month named after it

explanation.surface: A performance gets postponed until halfway through autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-October' gives the central O of OCTOBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of cowboy skills, a show.

clue.text: In assurance, tears madly around the Tyneside area

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation
madly says the letters of 'tears' are thrown wildly about

parts.note: NE, the North East of England, where Tyneside lies

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing wildly in the North East, despite reassurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' is the anagram signal and 'around' the container; Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a pledge or token given as a guarantee, an assurance.

clue.text: It's top gear for 23 ac.

parts.note: top gear reads as a car's highest gear, but it is headwear for the ranch man at 23 across

explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the wide-brimmed hat worn by cowboys, clothing for the head.
